articles.body:
Diplomatic Immunity is the eighth main quest of Skyrim , and it's pretty unique. Instead of delving into a dungeon or slaying a dragon, you're infiltrating a party to try to steal some Thalmor secrets.

Use the links below to jump to key steps in this quest:

Meet Malborn in Solitude and give him your equipment

Create a distraction and get away from the party

Search for information about the dragons returning

This quest begins as soon as Delphine sets off for Riverwood after A Blade In The Dark - you can either go with her or meet her there later. The plan is to hammer out the plan for infiltrating the Thalmor Embassy . You are to meet a trusted contact of Delphine’s named Malborn at Solitude .

Meet Malborn and Give Him Your Equipment

Solitude is in the northwest of Skyrim, not far from Morthal, which you'll have visited during The Horn of Jurgen Windcaller . You can either walk here or pay a carriage to take you to Solitude.

There's quite a lot you can do in and around Solitude, especially if you're making your way here on foot:

On the southern side of Dragon Bridge, the settlement to the southwest of Solitude, you can find two skill books - Mannimarco, King of Worms (alchemy) on an alchemy table and Warrior (block) at the small bandit camp.

The Break of Dawn side quest to unlock the Dawnbreaker sword at the shrine northeast of Dragon Bridge.

The Rear Guard (light armor) on a table in Castle Dour

The Gold Ribbon of Merit (archery) on a table in Fletcher's shop

The Refugees (light armor) in the blacksmith's shop

The Buying Game (speech) in a bookcase in the Bards College

Malborn is slinking about at The Winking Skeever, near the entrance to Solitude. There, Malborn will ask you which possessions you will need smuggled into the Thalmor Embassy (mainly your gear and some lockpicks would suffice).

Find Delphine at the stables outside Solitude and speak to her to receive some suitable party accoutrements. Speak once more to Delphine when you are ready to be whisked away to the Thalmor Embassy.

Upon your arrival, you meet a rather brazen bloke, Razelan. Keep him at the forefront of your mind. After showing your invitation to the Thalmor bouncer and exchanging pleasantries with the Ambassador, Malborn urges you to create a distraction so that you can sneak out.

Grab a Colovian Brandy either from Malborn or the waitress and hand one to Razelan. With his eyes wide, he pledges his loyalty to you, his best and most trusted friend. Ask him to create a distraction and slip out the back with Malborn.

Alternatively, you can talk to Erikur to create a distraction. After listening to his speech, he will begin to harass Brelas. Then, speak to him and offer to talk to her on his behalf. Do so, then return to Erikur and tell him that she said to meet her in her quarters. He'll then create a scene.

Return to Malborn to sneak into the kitchen. He will lead you into a room where you can find your gear. Once you retrieve your gear from the chest, it is up to you to fight off (or sneak past) the Thalmor guards in the back.

You'll have a few melee types and a wizard to contend with. Proceed ever closer to the quest marker, picking up various potions along the way.

You'll encounter more enemies outside, but your main goal is to head into Elenwen's Solar to fight Rulindil and remove his Interrogation Chamber Key . Use it to gain entry into the torture chamber and pilfer the Thalmier Dossier: Esbern from the chest.

After reading the dossiers, you will be instructed to leave the Embassy via the trap door in the torture chamber. You will need the Trap Door Key.

You'll need to wait for the guards that come in with Malborn to try to keep you from escaping. Kill the guards and loot the key off one of their bodies. Then open the trapdoor and leave.

The Reeking Cave, as this place is called, is home to a frost troll, but by this point you will have reunited with your followers (if you had any to begin with).

Simply return to Delphine at Riverwood at this point to complete the quest. You'll find her in the basement of the Sleeping Giant Inn, which is accessed through a false panel in the wardrobe of the room closest to the front counter. She'll then send you to find Esbern for the next quest, Cornered Rat .

articles.title: A Cornered Rat Walkthrough - The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Cornered Rat is the ninth main quest of Skyrim, and it begins immediately after Diplomatic Immunity, with Delphine sending you to Riften to find an old
articles.body:
A Cornered Rat is the ninth main quest of Skyrim , and it begins immediately after Diplomatic Immunity , with Delphine sending you to Riften to find an old accomplice named Esbern. Easier said than done, given he's hiding out in the sewers.

Rewards: There are no rewards for this quest.

Delphine recognizes the name Esbern in the Thalmor's files and figures the man is hiding out in Riften . You'll find Riften in the southeast of Skyrim, near Lake Honrich.

There are a few things to do in Riften while you're here:

Speak to Mjoll the Lioness in the tavern to recruit them as a Follower.

Complete The Book of Love side quest in the Temple of Mara.

The Armorers' Challenge (smithing) between the safe and dresser in The Scorched Hammer.

Purloined Shadows (pickpocketing) in Constance's bedroom in Honorhall Orphanage.

Surfeit of Thieves (lockpicking) and a Stone of Barenziah on the bedside table in the Jarl's Quarters.

Beggar (pickpocketing) on a table in The Ratway.

Esbern has major trust issues, so you will need to first speak to Brynjolf (if you haven't already, since he's part of the Thieves Guild questline. You'll find the guy in the outdoor market in the center of town.

Ask Brynjolf about Esbern and, being the shrewd businessman he is, he's not too keen on giving out free information.

If your Speech is high enough, the persuasion option may forgo the small favour he requires: A Chance Arrangement .

To complete A Chance Arrangement , you will need to sneak over to Madesi's stand, pick the novice lock, and steal Madesi's silver ring . Then you need to sneak to Brand-Shei, who's sitting on a pile of boxes, to place the ring in his inventory.

After finishing the quest, bring up Esbern again with Brynjolf, and he will admit to knowing your guy.

Enter the Ratway located under Riften. Expect to find hostile riffraff in these underground tunnels. Navigate through the Ratway until you reach the entrance to The Ragged Flagon.

You will find some Thalmor enemies in The Ragged Flagon. This multi-tiered, dank area leads to the Ratway Warrens, a holding place for some deranged folk, including Esbern.

When you find him, he denies being who you think he is. He continues to feign ignorance until you mention Delphine. If you recall, she told you to say something that would buy his confidence: "remember the 30th of Frostfall."

At that point, he lets you into his personal...living space. The quest ends after speaking to him and leads directly into the next main quest, Alduin's Wall .

articles.title: Bring Me the Head of Gustavo Orta Walkthrough - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This page is part of IGN's Cyberpunk 2077 Wiki guide and details everything you need to know about finding Gustavo Orta and convincing him to leave Night
articles.body:
This page is part of IGN's Cyberpunk 2077 Wiki guide and details everything you need to know about finding Gustavo Orta and convincing him to leave Night City in Bring Me the Head of Gustavo Orta .

Bring Me the Head of Gustavo Orta Walkthrough

To find Gustavo, enter the building on Pertrel St and use the elevator to reach the 32nd floor.

Once you reach the 32nd floor, you'll have a few options for getting to Orta:

Opening them will allow you to jump to a small, narrow ledge that will lead to a small balcony - if you have double jump unlocked, you'll have the ability to jump straight to Orta's balcony above.

Once you're on the balcony, crouch towards the door and turn right immediately, following the wall that features the windows. Using your quickhack, disable the nearby security camera and proceed up the stairs.

Neutralize Gustavo or Convince Him to Leave Town

Now that you've reached Gustavo Orta's room, head inside and speak with him, where you'll have the choice to either hear him out or to simply take his life. Note that convincing Gustavo to leave town will result in him taking his own life.

Which option you decide to choose is entirely up to you, but you should be warned: if you decide to neutralize Orta, you will need to fight your way through his men. We recommend hearing Orta out and giving him the option to leave Night City, as it removes the extra - and somewhat unnecessary - step of fighting Orta's men as you leave the building.

If you opt to hear Orta out and to allow him to leave Night City, he'll allow you to exit his apartment freely. Upon leaving his apartment and exiting the building, you'll complete the mission.

Up Next: Cyberpsycho Sighting: Phantom of Night City

articles.title: This smart home controller is literally a piece of wood
articles.summary: Mui’s screenless smart home controller uses touch and icons instead of voice or ads, but its $999 price keeps it niche.
articles.body: One of the fun parts of being a tech journalist for over a decade is that occasionally you get to watch a truly unique gadget go from concept to reality — and, eventually, into your living room. That’s the case with the Mui Board, a smart home controller built into a piece of wood. The Mui was first demoed at CES in 2019, and I’ve seen it at several shows over the years, in various iterations, always with the promise that it would ship soon. Well, this year it did (in limited quantities!), and I finally got to try one out in my living room. [Product: Mui Board | Wood with Wi-Fi [Image: The Mui Board is a screenless touch interface for my smart lights, Sonos speakers, and other devices. I installed it below these Nanoleaf panels, which also double as smart home buttons. You could call the Mui Board an anti-smart display. A Raspberry Pi-based smart home controller with Matter support, it’s just a piece of wood on your wall when not in use. But when you touch its capacitive surface, glowing dot-matrix icons appear, letting you control your music and lighting, set timers, view messages, and access other information you might use a smart display for. The idea is that technology should blend into your home — be calm, accessible, and integrated, not jarring or distracting. Mui is a Japanese term for being in harmony with nature, and the device is certified by the Calm Tech Institute. As someone surrounded by screens and smart displays in my home, I have long been intrigued by Mui’s alternative approach and was excited to try it out. [Video: mui board RSS feed] I’ve had the Mui Board second gen in my home for a few days now, and while I haven’t had a chance to fully put it through its paces, I’ve been impressed by its responsiveness, thoughtful design, and ambitious scope. The second-gen model debuted in 2023 but only became available for purchase earlier this year on Mui and Indiegogo. At $999 (on sale for $799), the Mui Board still feels closer to a beautifully realized concept than a mass-market product. It’s hard to imagine many people spending a thousand dollars on a smart home controller — but for the right person, it’s undeniably delightful. A simpler smart home controller [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Created by Japan-based Mui Labs, the Mui Board comes in two colors: natural maple or dark cherry. I am testing the maple version and have mounted it on the wall in my living room, just above my sofa. From there, I can reach up and tap it to see the time or weather, check what’s playing on my Sonos system, control my Hue lights, set a timer, and see the latest headlines from The Verge via a neat RSS feed feature. [Media: It’s a simple interface with minimalist icons that offer more control than you might expect at first glance. You can dim and turn lights on and off (no color changing), adjust a thermostat’s temperature, mode, and fan speed, open and close curtains and locks, and turn smart plugs on and off. What’s different from other smart home controllers with touch interfaces is that there are no ads, no chatty voice assistant, and no bright, distracting display vying for my attention. --- Specs: Mui Board * Price: $999 * Dimensions: 23 x 3 x 1 inches * Connectivity: Wi-Fi (2.4Ghz), BLE * Smart home protocols: Matter Controller, Echonet Lite, Web API * Installation: Wall-mounted * Hardware: Speaker and microphone --- Out of the box, the Mui Board connects to Wi-Fi and can display the time and weather. You can set timers, alarms, and reminders, and send messages to other Mui boards or the Mui app. It has two small built-in speakers and a microphone for recording messages, and is powered by an included AC adapter. Touching and drawing on the Mui Board is its best feature. It’s responsive and easy to use, and it has some delightful features. A small cat roams around the board and changes direction when you tap it. There’s a piano / drum mode that turns the board into a music machine, and you write messages on it by hand, not with a keyboard. It feels like technology you can play with. Smart home integrations [Image: The Mui Board is a great concept, and I found it useful, especially for controlling my Sonos speakers. But it does look a bit like a two-by-four on my wall. For smart home control, the Mui Board supports Matter and integrates with Sonos, Philips Hue, LIFX, SwitchBot, Ecobee, and Google Calendar APIs, among others, plus several Japanese services, including Radiko and the Echonet smart home protocol. Using the fairly simple Mui app, I connected the board to my Sonos system, and it displayed the title of the currently playing track, volume, and playback controls, and I could skip forward or back in my playlist. As a Matter controller, it can set up and control supported Matter devices directly, without using Amazon, Google, Apple, or similar services. It works with lighting, plugs, and thermostats, with locks next on the roadmap. It currently supports Matter over Wi-Fi, with Thread support planned. There’s no Thread radio onboard, so you’ll need a third-party border router. Lighting works best so far, while the other categories are still in limited testing. [Image: [Image: [Image: I successfully added a Meross Matter Wi-Fi smart plug directly to the board but struggled to pair some Matter devices, such as my Nest thermostat, using Matter’s multi-admin feature. I plan to do more testing here. I was able to connect my Hue lighting setup and could turn on and off all the lights or control each individually on the board. It was fairly slow, however, probably because I have a large Hue setup, and it was using the cloud API rather than a local connection. I really liked the Veil of Night feature that lets you draw a line on the board to set a timer that gradually dims the lighting. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Ultimately, the Mui Board is a big button / switch for controlling your smart home, with the benefit of icons to guide you to what you’re doing without a bright screen. As with any icon-based control, it takes a bit of learning to remember which icon does what, but you can customize the layout to put your most-used controls on the first screen and scroll through additional screens for more options. While I love the natural, furniture-like feel, when the board is off, it slightly resembles a two-by-four mounted on the wall — as if my husband abandoned a DIY project halfway through. A rounded edge, more sculptural profile, or small shelf accessory would go a long way toward softening the look. Also, there’s the issue of what to do with the cable. I installed the Mui in our living room, but after using it for a few days, I think the ideal place for this is in a bedroom, over a bedside table or headboard. That’s the room most people would like to keep screens out of, yet still want to control lights, locks, music, etc., without reaching for a phone or using voice. I don’t see using Mui Board exclusively as a smart home controller; its software doesn’t feel quite there yet for creating scenes and automations. But as an interface to your smart home, it’s a breath of fresh air. And as a fun device for controlling music, setting timers, and playing the piano, it’s successful, if very, very expensive. It’s been a slow burn to get the Mui Board to where it is today, and I’m intrigued to see where this thoughtful company takes its calm tech concept next. Mui Labs will be at CES again this year, where the company plans to debut a new well-being-focused sleep experience and “movement-based lighting control” for the Mui Board. Photos and video by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: I tested Apple’s hands-free Home Key — and it’s a big upgrade
articles.summary: Aqara’s new U400 smart lock is the first to use Apple’s UWB-based hands-free unlocking, and it works every time, even with full hands.
articles.body: Aqara has announced a new smart deadbolt lock at CES this week. The U400 ($269.99) is the first to support Apple’s Home Key’s hands-free unlocking. This uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach — no physical interaction required. I tested the U400 at my home earlier this month, and it’s been a significant upgrade for my front door. I still have to physically open the door, but there’s no need to punch in a code, use a fingerprint, pull out my phone, or bring my watch up to the lock; the door is unlocked by the time I get there. This makes it faster and easier to get into my house when my hands are full, if I’m wearing gloves, or if I’m just in a hurry. [Product: Aqara Smart Lock U400 | Hands-free unlocking isn’t new; I’ve tested several proprietary systems on locks from Yale, August, Level, and others. What’s different is the tech. Most existing systems use a mix of Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and geofencing and rely on you having an app running on your phone. I’ve also found them to be unreliable, often leaving me standing in front of a locked door waiting for it to open. [Media: Apple’s implementation uses Bluetooth and UWB to establish a direct connection between the lock and the phone — no app required. In my week of testing, it has worked every time without any waiting. Well, other than one incident when I had my phone under a pizza box. It still unlocked, but a beat after I arrived at the door. --- UWB-supported Apple devices Home Key’s Unlock on Approach hands-free unlocking works with the following Apple devices: * iPhone 11 and later, excluding iPhone SE (2nd and 3rd generation) and iPhone 16e, running iOS 18.5 or later * Apple Watch Series 6 and later, excluding Apple Watch SE, running watchOS 11.5 or later --- UWB is a short-range, low-power technology that uses short pulses across a wide frequency band and is designed for secure, real-time location, distance, and direction measurements. It’s already widely used to unlock cars. The technology is precise enough to understand which angle you are approaching from, so it won’t unlock if you’re inside the house or just walking past the front door. UWB unlocking is part of Apple Home Key, a feature of Apple’s Home app that lets you use your iPhone or Apple Watch as a key for your door when used with a compatible smart lock. Home Key locks that use NFC tap-to-unlock have been available since 2022, and we’ve tested several. Apple introduced UWB unlocking capability when iOS 18 launched in 2024, but there have been no compatible locks until now. I expect we’ll soon start to see more locks supporting it. UWB is part of a new universal smart lock standard called Aliro, being developed by Apple, Samsung, Google, and major lock manufacturers. Aliro is designed to bring both UWB and NFC unlocking to other smart home platforms and devices beyond Apple. This includes Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel phones and watches. The U400 is Aliro-ready, and the standard — announced in 2023 — is launching this year. At CES last year, a couple of UWB locks were announced, including ones from Schlage and U-tec. However, Aqara’s U400 is the first to confirm support for Apple’s Home Key implementation. The U400 is a full-replacement deadbolt smart lock that, along with Home Key (NFC or UWB), can be unlocked using a code on its touchscreen keypad, a fingerprint reader, or a traditional key. It’s a Matter-over-Thread lock, so you can control it with any Matter-compatible smart home app to add it to scenes and control it with a voice assistant. It also works with Aqara’s app via Bluetooth. --- Specs: Aqara U400 * Price: $269.99 * Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.2, Thread (Matter 1.4), NFC and UWB * Weatherproof rating: IP65 * Colors: Silver, black, satin nickel, shadow black * Dimensions: Inner panel: 7.01 × 2.99 × 1.85 inches / Outer panel: 6.58 × 2.99 × 1.01 inches * Power: Battery-powered; 4,880mAh rechargeable Li-ion battery * Battery life: Up to six months * Battery backup: Exterior USB-C charging port * Security rating: BHMA Grade 3 Certified * Replaceable cylinder: Yes --- The U400 has a built-in gyroscope that tells it whether the door is open or closed, and it can be set to automatically lock when closed. It’s IP65-rated and comes with a single 4,880mAh rechargeable battery, which Aqara says will last six months on a single charge. That’s on the low side for a Thread-powered lock, but UWB is a fairly power-hungry radio for a battery-powered device. Installing and setting up the U400 was straightforward and similar to most smart locks, other than the addition of a second data cable, which appears to power the UWB radio and antenna. The lock is larger and taller than Aqara’s other models, probably to accommodate the extra tech. I tested the silver model, and like most of Aqara’s devices, it’s more functional than design-forward. I’m not a fan of the Aqara logo at the bottom, and the large black touchscreen showed fingerprints right away. The exterior is aluminium and has a solid feel, but the large rear housing is all plastic. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I connected the lock to the Apple Home app by scanning the Matter code, and it onboarded smoothly. (It’s a Thread lock, so you need a Thread border router.) I already have Home Key set up, and Apple Home prompted me to use it with the U400 and to turn on Express Mode. This bypasses having to use Face or Touch ID to unlock a door, and it’s required for hands-free unlocking. While it unlocks using UWB, the U400 connects to your phone first via Bluetooth. Interestingly, the lock stayed connected to my Bluetooth whenever I was in the house. Because Home Key works with every member of my Apple Home household, my family’s iPhones all got updated to work with the U400 automatically. However, I had to activate Express Mode on each phone individually in the Home app and turn on Unlock on Approach on the Home Key in their Apple Wallet to get hands-free unlocking to work. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: You can add access codes to the lock via Apple Home, and the touchscreen keypad was responsive and easy to use. It’s very large, which means the numbers are well spaced, so it’s easy to hit the right buttons. If you connect the lock to the Aqara app, you can add codes and fingerprints. The fingerprint reader was fast and responsive, and it’s a good backup for when you don’t have your phone on you. [Image: The Aqara U400 Smart Lock I’ve been looking forward to UWB hands-free unlocking and its promise of a seamless, secure, and speedy way to unlock your door. Based on my experience so far, Aqara’s U400 delivers on that promise. While the lock is larger and less refined than some existing smart locks, Home Key UWB’s reliability and speed offer an exciting glimpse of where smart locks are headed. Photos and video by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: Book Formats - Dungeon Crawler Carl Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Dungeon Crawler Carl series first started as a web serial on Royal Road before Matt Dinniman decided to self-publish on Amazon back in September 2020.
articles.body:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl series first started as a web serial on Royal Road before Matt Dinniman decided to self-publish on Amazon back in September 2020. Since then the DCC books have gone through a series of different releases on various platforms. As of the most recent book release, all eight of the books are available as an eBook, a hardcover, and an audiobook.

Every Dungeon Crawler Carl book has first and foremost been released as an eBook. The initial release for every novel in the series is for the eBook version. In addition to being available to read for free via many libraries, you can also access all of the Kindle versions via a Kindle Unlimited subscription .

A Parade of Horribles was the first book in the series to get a hardcover release at the same time as the eBook version came out. This is largely because the publishing rights for the series weren't purchased by Penguin Random House until 2024, which is the same year hardcover editions started getting released.

Matt Dinniman self-published the first book as a paperback back in 2020, but it was the only novel in the series to get that treatment until 2025 when Penguin Random House started releasing copies with updated covers. The large print paperbacks are available for the first six books only, but smaller print editions started getting re-released at the end of 2025.

The Dungeon Crawler Carl audiobooks are some of the most popular audiobooks available in 2026, but they started getting released after the first books. Matt Dinniman said in an interview with IGN that he was well into writing book four when the first audio came out. It wasn't until A Parade of Horribles that the audiobook was released at the same time as the Kindle version.

Dungeon Crawler Carl, Vol. 1 (Graphic Novel)

Matt Dinniman, in collaboration with Vault Comics, has also started to release the graphic novel adaptation of his story. There has only been one volume released so far, but more are on the way. There's also a Crocodile spin-off set to release sometime in 2027. The main graphic novel collects chapters of the popular Webtoon version of the story.

The Dungeon Crawler Carl books are available in a variety of different formats , but most of those are just alternate versions of Matt Dinniman's written words. If you're looking for something a bit more visual, you're going to want to check out the graphic novel adaptations.

Dungeon Crawler Carl first started getting the comic book treatment back in July 2025 and has been getting weekly releases on Webtoon since then. Vault Comics has since collected these chapters into graphic novels, with the first two now available to buy.

Dungeon Crawler Carl, Vol. 1 (Graphic Novel)

articles.body:
Sprites are back again in the Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season. This time, they're pirate-themed and so far, there are 35 to find. This IGN guide lists all Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters, including all variants, rarities, and abilities, and all the Mastery Rewards. Use our Sprites Checklist to keep track of your collection!

All Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters - Sprite Checklist

There are currently 35 Sprites in Fortnite Treasure Hunters mini season, including 13 base Sprites plus variants. Use our checklist below to track your exact progress toward collecting and Mastering them all.

Halfpeel'd Sprite Rare Marks nearby eliminations on the map, with the radius increasing per level. Halfpeel'd Sprite

Barry O'Fish Sprite Rare Reduces sprint stamina drain when in water. Grants Slap effect at level 5. Barry O'Fish Sprite

Re-Pete Sprite Rare Increases your reload speed. Sometimes, reloading will also refund your ammo. Speed and ammo refund chance increases with each level. Re-Pete Sprite

Wayfinder Sprite Rare Reveals nearby Sprites and grants additional items when opening Buried Chests. Sprite detection radius increases with each level. Wayfinder Sprite

Exmarks Sprite Epic Reveals nearby Treasure Maps and Wanted Posters. Spawns a Treasure Map at level 5. Exmarks Sprite

Chester Sprite Epic Chance to get extra loot when opening Treasure Chests. Also nullifies fall damage. Increases your chance to get an additional item with each level. Chester Sprite

Lil' Squibbly Sprite Epic Automatically fishes a Fishing Hole when you jump into it and grants additional items, with more per level. Lil' Squibbly Sprite

Kelper Sprite Epic Replenishes your health over time when you're in water. Amount healed increases per level. Kelper Sprite

Lil' Flacko Sprite Legendary Creates a small shockwave when you land, which knocks back enemies. Knockback strength increased per level. Lil' Flacko Sprite

Lil' Uzi Vert Jr. Sprite Legendary Grants a Chug Splash effect when restoring Shields, with cooldown decreased per level. Lil' Uzi Vert Jr. Sprite

Plundarrgh Sprite Mythic Grants increased movement and pickaxe speed when opening chests. Plundarrgh Sprite

Transponder Snail Sprite Legendary Grants extra resources on pickup, with amount gained increasing per level up. Works for teammates, too. Transponder Snail Sprite

Sweet Dreams Sprite Mythic Grants extra resources on pickup, with amount gained increasing per level up. Works for teammates, too. Sweet Dreams Sprite

Like in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 3 and 4, most Sprites have Special, rarer variants which grant an additional effect. These variants include:

Cursed: Increases your chance of finding rare Sprite variants, but water damages you.

You unlock free rewards depending on how many Sprites you get to level five, AKA Master. There are currently 12 Sprite Mastery Rewards , with more on the way.

articles.title: Spirit Temple Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. After forging a tense alliance with the Gerudo people, Link has crossed the treacherous desert to arrive at the Evil Desert Colossus, the site of the Spirit Temple, but an unexpected road block will force Link to transcend time to gain the tools needed to find the Sage of Spirit.

Crossing the Mirage Desert, you'll arrive at the Spirit Temple and learn a melody to return here from Sheik. This melody will become incredibly important, as the entrance to this temple will bar you from progressing further unless you have the right tools, and one of those is inhabiting a much smaller body.

To enter the Spirit Temple, you'll first need to play the Prelude of Light to return to the Temple of Time, and leave the Master Sword behind to return to being a child. Before setting back off to the desert, be sure you've stopped by Zora River and claimed your last Magic Beans (which will cost 100 Rupees!), as well as Bug to be bottled.

As soon as you return to the Evil Desert Colossus, look to the left of the temple entrance to find the last patch of soft soil, where you can plant your last Magic Beans. Don't worry, you'll be coming back here as an adult before long.

Be sure to take one last bottled Bug and release it into the soft soil, and you can lure out a Gold Skulltula to defeat and get its token.

Now it's time to give this temple a fair shake. The entrance hall features two large plaques that clue you into what you'll need to get through each of the wings. There's also a line of statues on both sides (a few are actually Armos).

Direct your addition to the area that holds a small crawlspace you couldn't fit through as an adult. It seems that now, someone else is having a similar predicament. Approach, and you'll be introduced to the Gerudo Thief, Nabooru. She's a far cry from the "leader" the Gerudo Captain spoke so boldly of seven years in the future, but it seems her outspoken disdain for the "Gerudo King" has earned her a bit of a reputation.

She's searching for something to use against Ganondorf, but can't get past that giant stone on the other side of the entrance hall. This calls for a partnership, where you help her out by finding the treasure of this temple so she can use it to find a way deeper into the temple (because you're too young to wield giant gauntlets, right?).

When she steps aside, crawl through the space into the western wing. Dodge the spike traps, and be ready to deal with a few Fire Keese waiting in the rafters, while steering clear of a disguised Armos with a spike trap revolving around it. Toss a bomb over to it rather than get close to clear the room, opening up two gates.

There's another crawlspace to the north, but it leads directly to a locked door.

Take the northeast door first, where you'll find a pit with a mesh wall on the other side. Though you can't cross, you can take out some Keese hiding in the wall, and light two torches on this side with Din's Fire to match the lit torches on the far side, which will reveal a small Treasure Chest on the other side.

While you're on the southern side of this room, look along the mesh wall on the right side of a Gold Skulltula you can hit with your Boomerang.

Take the northeast door next, and you'll suddenly be locked in combat with a Stalfos. This guy is no longer an exclusive enemy for Adult Link, so you'll need to be very careful engaging him. He's got a much bigger reach than you, so you'll want to even the odds with every trick you can think of.

Bait out his large sweeping strikes and keep your distance until you see the Stalfos leap into the air with a lunging strike. Dodge around and get your stabs in, and use a Deku Nut or Boomerang to stun the foe when his guard is down, and follow up with Spin Attacks or Din's Fire.

Once the Stalfos goes down, look across the pit to spy a large yellow switch on the other side, blocked by a raised mesh bridge. Since you can hit it straight on, aim to the left and toss your Boomerang manually, and it will hit the switch as it returns to the right, lowering the bridge for you.

Be ready to block the advance of two Green Bubbles before slashing them apart as you cross the bridge, and then look for a small Treasure Chest in the corner guarded by Flying Pots that has a Red Rupee for you.

In the next room, you'll spot an interesting enemy. The stoic Anubis simply floats about and mirrors your movements. It won't even attack... unless you try to attack it first. It will block most anything you throw and emit magical projectiles, but it seems to be weak to fire, you'll just need to find a way to trap it instead of actively attacking it.

Look around the circular room for two small isolated platforms, and look along the edge of the northern one for a small eye switch you can hit with a Slingshot, which will activate a fire trap on the far platform. Since the Anubis is mirroring your movements, jump onto the platform on your side, and he'll follow straight into the fire and burn up, unlocking the nearby door.

Now you'll be back on the other side of the room you couldn't cross earlier. On this side, five Silver Rupees will appear around the small room, but first you'll want to deal with the ambushing Wallmaster and the Fire Keese here.

Once they've been defeated, climb the mesh walls and check the corners to collect all the five Silver Rupees, and open the chest you uncovered by lighting all torches to get your first Small Key.

Head through the northern crawlspace to an open the locked door to find a large mesh wall leading up to floor 2F. It's lined with a few Skullwalltulas, so be sure to knock them down with your Slingshot first before climbing up.

On this new level, you'll find yourself in a room with a large cracked wall with light peeking through toward a strange sun emblem on the floor. As you approach, two Lizalfos will appear to challenge you.

Don't be afraid to use all of your tools to their utmost to turn the tables on your opponents, like your Boomerang or Deku Nuts to stun, and following up with Din's Fire to catch both off guard.

When they've been defeated, turn your attention to a large yellow switch along the wall, and hit it to reveal a small Treasure Chest holding... Bombchus? It seems like someone is giving you a hint.

Stand by the sun emblem on the floor and face the crack, and let the Bombchus fly to ride up the wall (you can either clear the Skullwalltulas first or left the bombs blow them to pieces, and when the wall explodes, sun will shine on down, fully charging the emblem and unlocking the door!

This door leads to a massive chamber with another colossus statue sitting cross-legged, and towering up two entire stories from the second to the third floor! There's a lot to see and take in while in this room, but much of it is inaccessible due to your inability to use the Hookshot. Still, you can use a Deku Stick on the lit torch at the base of the statue, and light the opposite torch to reveal a large Treasure Chest holding the Dungeon Map!

While you're exploring the base of the statue, be sure to check the northeastern side, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula wedged in the corner that you can defeat.

Since there's not much else you can do, head up to floor 3F to find a barred door. Nearby, you'll find a switch in a recessed part of the floor that needs to be permanently stepped on to lower the gate.

Luckily, there's a small mesh wall nearby you can use to climb up to a ledge with a statue (not secretly an Armos, yay!), and push it down from the ledge and onto the switch to open the path.

Heading into the southwest room, you'll find it lousy with Beamos that will try and fry you with lasers if they get a clear shot. Use the high walls to take cover, and either dash around to toss a bomb, or set a Bombchu from a distance and let it crawl along and blow up out of the range of their lasers.

When the threats are gone, turn your attention to finding all five silver Rupees. There's one on a ledge behind the Beamos in the southeast (jump up from where the Beamos was sitting), and three more along the ledges in the center and northwest behind the other Beamos.

For the last silver Rupee near the center that's high up in the air, pull out one of the four stone blocks nearby so that it's right under the silver Rupee, then climb up and jump upward to claim it.

Before you go, pull out the other stone block with the sun emblem tucked away in the corner, and drag it down into the beam of light on the west side of the room. This will reveal a small Treasure Chest in the nearby alcove, which you can open to claim your second Small Key!

As you head through the door unlocked by gaining the silver Rupees, you'll come into a narrow corridor leading to the locked door you can open with the Small Key you just earned. Turn around before exiting this corridor, and you can find the last Gold Skulltula you can find in this temple as a child, hiding right above the doorway you just entered.

The room beyond has an imposing sight: A large Iron Knuckle sits in a chair clad in a suit of heavy armor, with a large double-bladed axe resting in its hand. As soon you make contact, the Iron Knuckle will spring to life to attack!

This foe is incredible dangerous, as its massive axe swings cannot be blocked with your shield. Instead, you'll need to rely completely on evasion and timing to avoid taking damage, which can be hard given the very short range of your Kokiri Sword.

The Iron Knuckle has two main attacks. When it raises its axe, it can quickly launch into two large sweeping side swings with a pause between each swing, each having a sizeable reach you'll want to backflip away from. The attack will cause the monster to stagger somewhat, giving you a few moments to race in and stab, but there's not a huge window of opportunity here.

The Iron Knuckle's second attack will have it quickly heave its axe behind its head before slamming down with full force in a vertical slam, which adds an impressive amount of reach to its attack. Dodging backward will not save you here, and you'll need to quickly detect the angle of attack and sidestep. This attack gives the largest window to counter, as the Iron Knuckle will need to pick its axe back up and readjust its position, giving you time to get in some meaningful hits.

With the terrible amount of damage this monster can do, playing defensively and evasively is a good bed. The good news is there are a few tricks that can help you survive this fight.

If you've taken a lot of damage in this encounter, lure the Iron Knuckle over to one of the many stone pillars. It's attack is massive enough to cleave through these pillars, which will all sprout Recovery Hearts for you to nab (so long as you wait for the next opening).

If trading blows with the armored foe simply isn't working for you, there are alternate approaches. While the Iron Knuckle is impervious to a lot of other forms of damage, it has no answer for explosives. This means with a good stockpile, you can send a train of Bombchus into the monster, or dodge around pillars to keep it at a distance while you lob bombs in the Iron Knuckle's direction!

Just be warned, the more damage you deal, the more of its armor will be destroyed, causing it to jog faster to close the distance on you.

With enough damage dealt over time, the Iron Knuckle will finally go down, unlocking the door behind him.

This path leads outside, onto the right hand of the Evil Desert Colossus statue! In this hand, it's holding a large Treasure Chest that contains the Silver Gauntlets! Whichever adult equips these will be capable of moving incredibly giant stones, like those large black stones you've seen blocking part of the temple!

Of course, Link and Navi are still totally committed to giving these to Nabooru, who calls down to you from below. Unfortunately, she'll soon be caught by Ganondorf's creepy witch minions, Kotake and Koume. I guess now you know why she never came back to the Gerudo Fortress after seven long years...

It seems a change of plans is in order. You won't be able to rescue Nabooru without going deeper into the Spirit Temple, and only an adult can wield the gauntlets. This means a return trip is in order, seven years from now!

Before you leave, you can walk along the ruined platform in the middle of the statue to find some Fairy Thoughts between two lit braziers. The fairy wishes the air wasn't so dry here, so bring a little moisture in with the Song of Storms, and you can get a well-deserved heal after that mini-boss fight with the Fairy Power.

Return to the Temple of Time using your Ocarina, and you'll get one last meeting with the owl, Kaepora Gaebora. He has nothing left to advise the Hero of Time, and you'll get a nice farewell as the strange owl takes to the skies. Take up the Master Sword to return to the future, equipped with your stylish new Silver Gauntlets.

When you warp back to the Evil Desert Colossus, there's a few things to take note of. There's a large black rock on the northern side of the desert here, and you can lift it aside to reveal a Grotto full of enemies you can blast to reveal a Purple Rupee.

If you planted that last Magic Bean by the temple entrance, you can now ride the magic floating plant here. It will do a wide loop of the desert area here, and as it passes by the second of two small plateaus, you can jump off and wait for night to fall for a Gold Skulltula to appear here!

The magic floating plant you grew leads to more than one secret. By now you've probably seen the shimmering Heart Piece on top of the rock archway in front of the temple. Ride the plant for the entirety of its long trip around the desert, and it will finally stop at the archway, allowing you to pick up the last Piece of Heart in the game! Once you've cleared the Spirit Temple, you'll have a full set of Heart Containers!

Entering the Spirit Temple once again, you now have a whole new section to explore. With your Silver Gauntlets, the large black rock slab can be pushed backward, opening a path to the dungeon's east wing.

You'll encounter a similar entrance to the west wing here, with three doorways (the middle is locked), and a switch above the Beamos in the center you can destroy with a well-placed bomb. Hitting the switch will open both doors on the side, so take the northwest door first.

You'll have to fend off a Wolfos in here, which you can test out the Biggoron Sword if you got it by slashing its back after it tries to swipe at you. Once it's defeated, you can spy a ledge on the other side of a sandy pit, and the insignia of the Royal Family on the nearby ledge (odd place to shout out the Royal Family?) Play Zelda's Lullaby, and a large Treasure Chest will appear on the far platform, which you can grapple to with the Longshot to gain the Compass!

Head back into the previous room, and take the northeast door this time. This room is full of rolling boulders that cross from one side of the room to the other, proving a tricky hazard to navigate. There are also 5 silver Rupees to collect in this room while dodging the boulders!

To get the first silver Rupee, put on your Hover Boots, and walk off the ledge in the center to run into it before dropping (just make sure the boulder below is off to the side).

The other four silver Rupees are each found in the small alcoves at the end of where the three boulders roll between. Move carefully to avoid them and you clamber up into each spot.

Before playing the Song of Time to move a blue block and reveal the last silver Rupee, check the alcove in the far northwest corner to find a Gold Skulltula hiding away in this dark corner.

With the gate unlocked, enter the door to find a Like Like guarding a small chest with a Small Key inside. Quickly stun the monster with your Hookshot, and try using a fully charged spin attack from the Biggoron sword to tear it apart in one blast.

Return back to the main room of the east wing and head north through the door you can now unlock. Another Like Like will be waiting here, but keep your distance and wait for the Flying Pots to come at you first before focusing your attacks on the monster so it doesn't gobble up your items!

Climbing up to floor 2F, there will be a large room full of lights, and a mysterious green energy that will try to slam into you! Put on the Lenses of Truth to reveal a Floormaster whose been hiding in the room, and take it out when the green glow fades, and throw in a spin attack to eliminate all the tiny hands that pop out.

Now you can turn your attention to the light streaming through the room, hitting a contraption in the middle with a mirror that reflect light against the wall. You can turn it, moving the beam of light to hit several sun emblems along the eastern side of the wall that each unlock something... not all of them good.

From left to right, the easternmost sun emblem unlocks a small Treasure Chest with 5 Bombs, while the next one summons another Wallmaster to deal with. Past that, the next emblem directly to the south unlocks the nearby door, while the final sun emblem drops a chest.

Don't be too hasty to open it -- according to your Compass, there was only one chest in this room. If you look closely, the chest even flaps open from time to time, much like the fake doors in the Fire Temple. This chest is also fake, and will hit you with a freezing trap if you try to open it normally, so smash it or leave it be.

Now you'll finally be back in the main temple statue room that you explored as a child, only now you'll have access to the full room to explore!

Start by dropping down to the base of the statue, and using your Longshot to zip up to the statue's left hand on the east side of the room. Zip up to a ledge in the northeast corner to find a large pressure plate you can smack with the Megaton Hammer, unlocking the central door down below.

From this vantage point, looking back at the statue hand you clambered up to reveals that it also has the sigil of the Royal Family. Drop back down and play Zelda's Lullaby, and a small Treasure Chest will appear on the opposite hand holding a Small Key!

While you're on the hand on the west side of the room, look up for a high ledge where a gust of straw is blowing. Play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre, and latch onto him with the Longshot. He's placed right by the last Gold Skulltula in this temple, which should put you at 99!

Be sure to check the middle door at the base of the statue for a shortcut leading back down to the temple's entrance you can uncover by pushing aside some black stone slabs, then head up to floor 3F of the large statue room on the east side (there's a hookshot target on the underside of the balcony), using your new key to open the door.

Dart past or destroy the Beamos before heading to a new room where you'll be met with another Anubis, as well as a Beamos that will try to give you trouble from its platform across the pit. You can move to the ledge and toss a Bomb that should land right in front of it, and then worry about the Anubis... and his friends.

Two more Anubis will appear from the walls as you move closer to the center of the room, providing a tricky problem in how to defeat them all. Even as an adult, none of your attacks will work, so you'll need to resort to trapping them in a fire pit instead.

Head to the eastern side of the room to find a pressure plate to stand on that ignites the fire pit, but the location of each Anubis relative to yours means luring them to the fire won't be straightforward.

To kill the first, return to the northwest corner of the room and stand on the small ledge leading to the four central platforms. Then, to defeat the second, jump across to the southwest corner and walk west until the next Anubis is burned.

The last one seems to not move toward the pit with any available spot you can move yourself, so you'll need to create a new place to move. Look for the large blue block along the wall and play the Song of Time near it. This will summon a blue block into the south part of the room, and you can leap to it to make the last Anubis rush over to the fire pit, unlocking the eastern door.

The large corridor beyond features doors in two directions. The one to the north is locked by a light puzzle, but there's no way to redirect light here. Instead, focus on the pressure plate in the recess in front of you. You'll need something to stay on it, but the nearby statue is actually an Armos... but that can still work!

Lure the Armos into lunging at you from across the recess, and it will fall down into the pit and be unable to escape, opening up the southern door for you! Don't worry if you accidentally get freaked out and bomb the Armos by mistake, as a new one will appear shortly afterward.

Head through the southern door into a corridor with two invisible small Treasure Chests that you can view with the Lenses of Truth, holding a Red Rupee in each of them.

Entering the next room, you'll have an Iron Knuckle rematch! Even though you're much bigger now, that doesn't mean this miniboss will be a pushover. Most of your tools (aside from bombs) still have little effect, but since defense doesn't help a whole lot, it's more reason to swap to the Biggoron Sword for all-out offense after dodging the monster's attacks.

Skirt around the edge of the Iron Knuckle's range, and either give a quick poke after its two side slashes, or dodge to the side of the overhand swing and get up close for a jump attack of your own!

If things get dicey, you can always retreat behind the pillars for a breather and use the hearts that come out when they are attacked to heal back up, or toss explosives well out of range.

When this Iron Knuckle goes down, you'll be able to exit to the temple exterior again, this time on the statue's left hand. Step on the pressure plate to reveal a second large Treasure Chest out here, and this one contains yet another special treasure -- the Mirror Shield!

With this special polished shield, you'll be able to reflect certain elements back at attackers, and also maneuver beams of light!

Try it out by returning to the previous corridor and heading up to the area with a beam of sunlight in front of a sealed door. Hold your shield out with ZL, and then use the right control stick to angle the beam of light upward to the sun emblem above the door, which will unseal it. Beyond, you'll find your next Small Key.

Return west to the room where you had to burn away the three Anubis, and unlock the door here to continue west. As you enter, you'll be faced with two Beamos at close range! Trying to pull out a bomb may still get you zapped while you wait for it to explode, so why not try out your new Mirror Shield?

Ready your shield and when the first Beamos notices you, its laser will reflect off your shield! You can actually control the beam with the control stick to explode the second Beamos, before reflecting it back on the first one to defeat the pair!

Ahead, there is a series of high moving mesh walls with spikes along the side. The moving walls will bring the mesh into the spikes, so you'll need to move quickly. Better yet -- just use the Longshot on the top of ledge while the mesh is in the middle to bypass it!

Up on the halfway point, you'll have to deal with two cagey Lizalfos who will scurry about to try and jump over and attack from behind, but won't last long against the might of a Biggoron Sword.

Once they fall, there's a much higher mesh wall to climb, which you can still mostly bypass using your Longshot.

Upon reaching floor 4F, you'll be met with a sealed door in front of you, and a series of chambers off to the west. Don't leave this area yet, and instead note the symbol of the Royal Family before the door. You can play Zelda's Lullaby here to unseal the door.

This leads to a chamber with the blue Treasure Chest that holds the Boss Key... but it's completely on fire! Doors line the chamber, but looking at them for a moment you'll quickly realize all of these doors are actually fake!

Use the Megaton Hammer to first squash the few Lava Slugs wandering by the fiery chest, and then take the hammer to each of the doors to break them apart so they can't fall on you. In doing so, you'll find that one of the doors on the northern side was hiding an eye panel, which you can shoot to lower a mesh gate above you.

Use your Longshot to zip up above the platform to fall onto the walkway, and then head to the other side to step on the pressure plate, dousing the flames so you can claim the Boss Key!

Now all you need to do is find the final boss itself. Head up the ledge to the area to the west. There's a large reflective panel along the ceiling here, but nothing to reflect off yet.

Hop down from the high ledge and look south to find a large switch you can hit, unsealing the door further west.

This leads to a series of connected rooms that holds a large ray of light, which you'll need to find a way to direct into the previous room through the bars on the south side. First however, stand in the first room and reflect the light back on sun emblem over the doorway, revealing a small Treasure Chest with five Bombs.

Several White Bubbles float around a mirror device in the next area, which you can hit from afar to knock out their flames before finishing them off. Once they've been dealt with, bomb the cracked wall to the east to reveal a new path to reflect the light into that's streaming in from above.

This last room has one more mirror contraption, guarded by two Dinolfos. They're a bit tougher than the Lizalfos, so don't get too over-eager in your fight that you end up taking too much damage. Watch for their patented jump attack from behind and counter with your own as each of them approaches, or use your Deku Nuts or Longshot to stun them so they can't evade a large spin attack!

When the two Dinolfos have fallen, angle this new mirror that's catching the light from the previous room to head north back into the chamber with the tilted mirror, which will now be transferring the light straight down!

Return to that room and drop down, and then look for a small sun emblem on the wall to the side to hit with your Mirror Shield. This will activate a lift, lowering the platform your on that's bathed in light down to the room with the large statue below.

You'll now be right in front of the statue's face, which has the same marking as the sun emblems you've been filling with light. Do the same to the large statue face with your Mirror Shield, and the face will crumble away to reveal the path to the boss!

Before you can face Koume and Kotake however, you'll have to contend with their prized puppet, clad in a suit of black armor. This Iron Knuckle may seem a bit odd, but it's still just as dangerous! That being said, you won't have to deal as much damage to this one as you have the rest -- you just need to break off its armor. Use your Biggoron Sword after dodging to the side to inflict a ton of damage, or hang back and let the Bombchus roll if you want to have some fun.

When the armor falls away, you'll be met with a familiar face. The reunion will be short-lived, as Koume and Kotake return to take their puppet back under their control, and goad you into chasing them through the next door. Might as well oblige them.

The two Witch Sisters are Ganondorf's most loyal minions, and they boast some extreme magical talen. One can utilize incredible fire magic, while the other has developed powerful frost spells. These spells have influenced their look, so be sure to keep track of which one deals in fire, and which in frost.

As the two sisters fly around the arena and circle you on their broomsticks, you can spot the hue of their magic shields. They are impervious to any attack you can think to throw at them -- even Fire or Ice Arrows! Instead, the only magic that can pierce their defenses is their own! Due to the nature of this fight, you won't need your sword right now, and since the Biggoron Sword doesn't let you shield if you accidentally have it out in front of you, it's better to equip the Master Sword just in case.

Keep an eye on both until one of them begins to summon a magic sigil in the air in front of them, signaling that they are going to attack next. When they stop, stand in the middle of the arena and keep your shield targeted on the attacker.

When they try to hit you with an elemental beam, you'll be able to reflect it entirely! However, their shield protects themselves against their own magic type, but not the others. The Witch Sister that's not attacking will float close by, giving you the chance to angle your beam right into them to deal some damage!

You'll have to successfully pull this off three times, but the Witch Sisters aren't entirely dumb. They'll start to fake-out which one of them is preparing the next spell, so if you see their magic sigil disappear, it means the other one is getting ready to ambush you. The one who isn't attacking will also try to avoid the beam you're reflecting -- first they'll try floating in a different direction, and later on they may even teleport to the other side, so keep following their path to cut them off.

Once they've been hit a few times, the Witch Sisters will decide to kick things up a notch, showcasing their ultimate move by combining into one being: Twinrova!

As the combined might of both Witch Sisters, Twinrova is more agile and deadly in this new form, and can use both fire and ice magic. The same rules still apply however -- one magic is capable of breaking through her defenses as long as you get enough of it.

This time, she'll fly high up into the air above one of the smaller platforms, raising one of her two magic wands before sending an elemetal blast your way. Block it with your Mirror Shield, and the energy will be stored in the shield as it begins to glow. You'll need to store more energy before you have enough to fully blast it back at Twinrova: Three times, in fact.

This is where things get a bit tricky. Twinrova will continue this pattern of floating around before picking an element to attack you with, but you want to only fully block one specific element at a time: Either three fire blasts, or three ice blasts.

If you see her preparing a blast opposite the one being stored in your shield, you'll instead need to dash out of the way. Both fire and ice spells from Twinrova will leave a lasting mark on the main platform until she fires again, so be mindful of the residue while you continue to strafe and evade.

Once she's fired three of the same element, your Mirror Shield will bounce the energy back at Twinrova. It will shatter her shield, sending her down to the small platforms. This is your chance to leap across and start slashing away. We recommend briefly swapping to the Hover Boots rather than wasting time jumping, and then attack with the Biggoron Sword for maximum damage.

When she flies up in the air, make sure your sword is put away and the shield is back out for the next charge.

Eventually, Twinrova will start trying to change things up. She'll fake out her next move by raising a wand but then lowering it and raising the opposite instead. She can also fly farther back to a corner of the room before jetting forward like Phantom Ganon to spiral through the arena in a divebomb attack. If you're worried about getting hit, simply jump off the platform and then climb back up.

The rest of the fight comes down to patience and reacting quickly. Don't be fooled by her magic switch-up, or you'll risk negating the progress of charging up your shield. You'll only need to break her shield and knock her down a few times to deliver the final blow!

Once Twinrova falls, Koume and Kotake will take an unexpected trip up into the sky, leaving you to claim the final Heart Container, which should put you at a full 20 Hearts!

Step into the light to meet the final Sage, and gain her resolve to fight against Ganondorf to the very end with the Spirit Medallion. At this point. All five sages will have awakened and be ready to aid you in your final attack against the Demon King. You need only meet with one last person at the Temple of Time to proceed...

Before you do that, it's worth making a few last stops before we get to the finale!

For starters, you can now lift up any other large black rock slabs you may have noticed, like the quarry room in Goron City, which hides one final Treasure Chest with a Purple Rupee.

You should also head back to Zora Fountain, and look over by the Great Fairy's Fountain for more black stone slabs to remove, revealing a small tunnel path. Be warned, it's full of invisible Skulltulas and you'll need to advance carefully. The very top of the cave leads to an overlook, and once nightfall, the last Gold Skulltula will appear!

The curse is now ready to be lifted! Return to the Cursed Spider House to witness the father be finally cured and turn back into a normal person once again. As thanks for all of your incredible work, you'll be gifted a Gold Rupee worth 200. That's not the best part: You can talk to the man as many times as you wish, and he'll keep giving you more, effectively giving you infinite money! Be sure to use it well to stock up on Blue Potions and other supplies!

If you haven't already, be sure to also seek out and complete the Gerudo Training Grounds now that you have the Silver Gauntlets to get all the keys inside, and you'll have an easier time claiming its prize: The Ice Arrows.

Once you feel you're ready to take the fight to the Demon King, head back to the Temple of Time to meet with the one you've been waiting to see.

articles.title: Marvel Star Xochitl Gomez Says She Struggled to Find Work After Joining the MCU as Everyone Assumed She'd Be Too Busy — Even Though Her Character Has Never Returned
articles.summary: Xochitl Gomez has described her big Marvel break as "a gift and a curse," after struggling to find further acting work since appearing in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.
articles.body:
Xochitl Gomez has described her big Marvel break as "a gift and a curse," after struggling to find further acting work since appearing in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness .

Gomez got her acting break on Disney series Raven's Home and Netflix show The Baby-Sitters Club, before being cast in 2022's Doctor Strange sequel as America Chavez. Since then, however, her acting output has been limited, though she did take part (and win) the 2023 season of Dancing with the Stars.

Speaking to Bustle , Gomez said her MCU role as the multiverse-punching teenager had dissuaded filmmakers from casting her in other projects — and that despite seeking other work, she had suffered from the assumption that she'd now become too expensive to hire or, alternatively, that she would be unavailable due to her potentially being busy filming further Marvel appearances.

The Most Surprising Avengers and Marvel Characters Not Announced for Doomsday

"After [Doctor Strange], I had a hard time getting roles," Gomez told . "They were like, 'She's too expensive. What if she's in this and that, her schedule?' And I'm like, 'Guys...'

"It was a gift and a curse," she continued, "because I was like, 'Wait, I want to do the cool indie movies. Give me a chance, guys.'"

It's something of an odd situation as, in reality, Gomez has not returned as America Chavez in any subsequent Marvel project, despite her portrayal of the character being generally well received.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness ends with Chavez heading off to train alongside other sorcerers at Kamar-Taj, seemingly setting up her up as an even more powerful superhero when she next pops up. Four years later, however, and there's been no mention of her ever turning up again. For a while, rumors persisted that Marvel was considering a magical school series entitled Strange Academy that may have continued the Kamar-Taj storyline, but nothing is yet to materialize.

There's been no confirmation of Chavez turning up in Avengers: Doomsday or the subesequent Avengers: Secret Wars, either, despite her multiversal powers seemingly being a good fit for a pair of movies that are set to wrap up the MCU's Multiverse Saga. But perhaps her return is being kept as a surprise?

"Well, they own the rights to my image, so it's possible," Gomez concluded, when asked if she would appear in Doomsday next month.

articles.title: Being Heumann Is a Mawkish But Crowd-Pleasing and Authentic Look at the Work of Disability Advocate Judith Heumann
articles.summary: Being Heumann review: A hilarious, mawkish crowd-pleaser about disability advocates, cast with authenticity.
articles.body:
Being Heumann is in theaters now and debuts November 13 on Apple TV.

Disability activist Judith Heumann has the perfect name for a story about forcing politicians to acknowledge the humanity of an underclass. More perfect still is the title of her memoir, Being Heumann, which CODA director Sian Heder turns into a straightforward but occasionally rousing biopic revolving around a political sit-in, a film whose authentic casting is a vital part of its form.

Beginning with a failed streetside protest in 1972, the movie zips forward several years into the work of a bustling coalition with busy offices. The year is 1977, and the wheelchair-using Heumann, aka Judy (Ruth Madeley, a wheelchair-user herself), is among a group of several protesters furious with the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare’s (HEW) preening secretary Joseph Califano Jr. (Mark Ruffalo) for refusing to sign a vital equality act into law. Some in Judy’s camp are blind or Deaf; others are para- or quadriplegic; and a small handful are able-bodied allies from queer or racial advocacy groups like the Black Panthers. As they gather outside the HEW offices in San Francisco, Judy makes impromptu demands for a building occupation until Califano Jr. signs the aforementioned legislation, referred to as “Section 504.”

There is, however, a moral wrinkle to Judy's plan. Her cohorts soon discover that she packed a toothbrush; it was always her plan to enter the building and stay overnight. That the fierce equality advocate refused to share this with her protesters makes her self-absorbed in a particularly compelling way, as her eyes are gradually opened to the ways in which her actions do or do not gel with her fellow protesters. Among them is the fellow polio-stricken Ed Roberts (Michael Patrick Thornton), who can’t join this leveling-up of Judy’s praxis because he needs to sleep in an iron lung. Roberts’ role is therefore minor, but the frankness with which Thornton performs it makes him an absolute must-watch.

This is true for practically the entire cast, beginning with Judy herself, who Madeley imbues with a fearsome, acerbic, and headstrong attitude that slowly reveals deep insecurities as her fellow advocates — including soft-spoken organization newcomer Kitty Cone (Madeline Delp) — push back on her methods during the occupation, yielding entertaining skirmishes. The movie’s tone, therefore, veers between challenging, comedic, and broadly uplifting, as its focus falls on numerous in-group debates and conversations while the activist contingent waits for the targets of their protests to respond.

While the film occasionally leans towards prescriptive and verbose — its scenes often pivot around characters having to explain their views in detail — this is part and parcel of Heder’s particular telling, which aims to bring crisscrossing political debates about disability activism to the fore. Being Heumann is at its most interesting when its many heroic subjects disagree, a prickliness which eventually leads to a greater cooperation down the line.

The real sit-in lasted nearly four weeks, and Heder details every challenge along the way as able-bodied allies like Dylan O’Brien’s news reporter, Evan White, and Ray Fisher’s Panther member, Chuck Jackson, embed themselves with the group to assist and observe while supportive politicians like Congressman George Miller (Rob Delaney) assist from the outside. This, too, ends up a meta-textual piece of the movie’s telling; these relatively well-known actors are the kind that get smaller-budgeted movies green-lit, and that they cede space to the central cast feels in and of itself like an act of allyship.

The ensemble is made up of relative unknowns, and that their own disabilities are in line with those of their characters serves a dual purpose. The first is verisimilitude: Freed from the constraints of having to concentrate on “performing” disability, they each bring a remarkable and personable realism to their roles, including Andrew Pilkington as Hale Zukas, a nonverbal activist with cerebral palsy who communicates with a helmet-mounted pointer and a board full of letters. That he spells out each word slowly is no hurdle to the character’s sharp, sarcastic wit (“Disability is not a tragedy,” he spells, as a fellow protester interprets for the larger group. “It is a tremendous hassle.”). Similarly, when we catch glimpses of Judy’s morning routine, involving being helped to the bathroom by an attendant who shows up rather late, her understandably rankled attitude takes center stage, both fleshing her out as a character while fueling her advocacy in the first place.

The second and equally important purpose of casting disabled actors is as an act of equity. Section 504 may be about ramps for wheelchair-users, readers for the blind, interpreters for the Deaf, and so on — a costly endeavor according to Califano Jr. — but its real goal is equal access to jobs and education. Nearly every character on screen occupies the HEW building because they’ve been denied opportunities owing to their disabilities (Judy, for instance, was denied her teaching license). So, granting these roles to disabled actors, which they might ordinarily lose to able-bodied peers who have had more chances to bolster their résumés, is the movie putting its money where its mouth is. Califano Jr. complains about being asked to remake the world, but the production does it with ease.

Since the film is a large ensemble piece, Heder makes minor alterations to traditional framing; her eye-level medium and group shots are much closer to the ground to accommodate the wheelchair-using cast, and the frame expands laterally to capture them. These are only minor adjustments, but they speak to the fluidity of Heder’s filmmaking, wherein she tells broad and familiar stories by changing their packaging ever-so-slightly. Similarly, her Best Picture winner, CODA, not only casts real Deaf adults in major roles, but the movie’s editing follows the rhythm of their signed dialogue rather than the traditional beats of spoken words. And, much like CODA, Being Heumann doesn’t shy away from the full dimensions of is disabled subjects, including their sex lives; in the process, it makes the sit-in seem pretty fun and hedonistic.

Heder’s minor departures help contort the screen to include a wider array of people within the bounds of a traditionally mawkish but no less effective political biopic. Granted, a handful of beats remain too obvious and on-the-nose to really work — like the out-of-place use of the Ramones’ “Judy is a Punk” accompanied by slow-motion wheelchair-rolling — but the movie is ultimately a crowd-pleasing delight, which is the sort of thing Heder excels at making.

articles.title: Nintendo Announces 2026 Black Friday Sale, Including $50 Switch 2 Bundle Discount
articles.summary: Nintendo has officially confirmed that Switch 2 consoles will be on sale and discounted for Black Friday this year. Here's everything you need to know about Nintendo's upcoming Black Friday 2026 sale, including the start time, deal lineup, price, and more.
articles.body:
Nintendo has officially announced details for its 2026 Black Friday sale , including a brand-new offer on Switch 2 consoles, $20 off MSRP on select Nintendo Switch 2 games, and more.

The sale will start on Nov. 22, and will headline with a $50 discount on Nintendo Switch 2's Mario Kart World console bundle . With an MSRP of $549.99, that brings it down to $499.99.

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

The sale will last through Nov.29, but Nintendo has also confirmed that the Switch 2 bundle offer will extend through Dec. 5, offering fans a bit more time to secure the deal.

We have a few confirmed games that will be included in the sale so far: Donkey Kong Bananza, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, Kirby AirRiders, Super Mario Galaxy 1+2, and Super Mario Party Jamboree. As mentioned, these will be $20 off MSRP and start at $39.99 while the sale is on.

Don't get ahead of yourself, however, as while the $39.99 price sounds great, it is more than likely Donkey Kong Bananza will be $49.99 for Switch 2, as its current MSRP in the US is still $69.99.

Nintendo has also confirmed that Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Target, GameStop, and the official Nintendo Store will carry these offers during the Black Friday sales at each respective retailer.

As a reminder, earlier this year, Nintendo announced a price rise for the Switch 2 in the US and other international markets. In the US, this increased the price from $449.99 to $499.99 in September 2026.

Following this, Nintendo also revealed its new Switch 2 bundles , priced at $549.99, including either Mario Kart World or Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. These bundles also include a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, which in total brings savings of $37.98, at least according to Nintendo.

Now with the aforementioned Black Friday discount applied, savings are closer to $88 in total for the Mario Kart bundle , while the Switch Sports Resort bundle will stay at $529.99.

This is the first official discount the Nintendo Switch 2 has received since it first launch in June 2025.

We saw a surprise discount on a similar Mario Kart World bundle during Black Friday last year , but as far as we're aware, this was led by retailers like Walmart and Amazon, rather than Nintendo itself.

Down to $449.99, this included both the Switch 2 console and Mario Kart, but didn't include the Nintendo Switch Online membership.

While the Switch 2 is on sale in the US this year, it's effectively wiping away the $50 price hike from September. Whether or not you see that as a deal is your own prerogative.

We've already seen some fairly good Switch 2 deals in the run up to Black Friday as well, including one giant discount at AliExpress , and another for new customers at Woot . But, if you'd prefer to wait it out for the official deal from Nintendo, that's a reasonable move as well.

Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27?

Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before what I like to call "Black Friday proper."

Having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a Switch deal hits (like it is on November 22), it usually sticks for the rest of the sale. That means the prices you see now on consoles, games, and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to December. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer.

These offers are reliable, worthwhile, and unlikely to get any better. Grab the games and hardware you’ve had your eye on, there’s no risk of Black Friday regret, only the satisfaction of finally getting exactly what you wanted at a price that makes sense.

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV

ICYMI: Walmart's Black Friday sale has also officially started , with the major US retailer's "Black Friday - Event 1" discounts now live. That's alongside Best Buy's early Black Friday sale , which went live last week (lasting through to Nov. 19), alongside the announcement of Amazon's official sale that starts on Nov. 19. So we're definitely into the full swing of things now.

Are you planning to pick up anything in Nintendo's Black Friday sale? Let us know in the comments, and stick around with IGN as we continue to update you daily on the best Black Friday deals for 2026.
